transcript.text: Welcome. In this short lesson we will find out what happens when an acid meets a base.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Before any experiment, put on a lab coat, gloves and safety goggles.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Acids and bases can damage your skin and eyes.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Here a scientist pours a solution in the lab.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: An acid such as hydrochloric acid releases hydrogen ions in water.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: A base such as sodium hydroxide releases hydroxide ions.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: When the two solutions are mixed, each hydrogen ion joins a hydroxide ion to form water.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: The sodium and chloride ions that remain make table salt, which stays dissolved.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: An indicator shows when the reaction is complete.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Universal indicator turns green at pH seven, which is neutral.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Accidents can happen in any lab.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: If glassware breaks, never pick up the sharp pieces with your hands.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: Tell your teacher and sweep them up with a brush and dustpan.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: So, an acid plus a base gives a salt plus water.
transcript.speaker: narrator

transcript.text: This reaction is called neutralization, and antacid tablets use it to settle an upset stomach.
transcript.speaker: narrator

reasons.guardian: fixture: sharp shards could cut a child

concept_nodes.label: Personal Protective Equipment
concept_nodes.summary: Wear a lab coat, gloves and safety goggles because acids and bases can damage skin and eyes.

concept_nodes.label: Acid Dissociation
concept_nodes.summary: An acid such as hydrochloric acid releases hydrogen ions when it dissolves in water.

concept_nodes.label: Base Dissociation
concept_nodes.summary: A base such as sodium hydroxide releases hydroxide ions in water.

concept_nodes.label: Neutralization Reaction
concept_nodes.summary: Hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions combine to form water; the remaining ions form a dissolved salt.

concept_nodes.label: Indicator and Neutral pH
concept_nodes.summary: Universal indicator shows when neutralization is complete by turning green at pH 7.

concept_nodes.label: Safe Handling of Broken Glass
concept_nodes.summary: Never pick up broken glass by hand; tell the teacher and use a brush and dustpan.

thread_roles.gist: What acids and bases release in water
Hydrogen and hydroxide ions form water and salt
What to do when glassware breaks
Acid plus base gives salt plus water

quiz_bank.stem: Which ion released by sodium hydroxide later combines with hydrogen ions?

quiz_bank.rationale: An acid plus a base gives a salt plus water.

quiz_bank.stem: What forms when a hydrogen ion joins a hydroxide ion?

quiz_bank.stem: After neutralizing hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide, what happens to the salt formed?

It falls out as a solid

quiz_bank.stem: What colour does universal indicator turn at pH 7?

quiz_bank.stem: What does pH 7 mean, according to the lesson?
Why is an indicator used during neutralization?

quiz_bank.rationale: An indicator shows when the reaction is complete.

Pick up the pieces with your hands

quiz_bank.stem: Which tools does the lesson recommend for cleaning up broken glass?
